attributes.action: Death should not be a defence against child abuse allegations
attributes.additional_details: Currently the death of a child sexual abuser can be used to prevent civil prosecution of a school or organisation under vicarious liability laws in Scotland. This situation means that if that survivor is the only one to come forward with regard to that abuser the organisation can avoid prosecution by claiming the inability to mount a defence because the perpetrator is deceased. This results is a two tier situation where the survivor is effectively treated with less regard and poorer outcomes.
attributes.background: The death of a child abuser should not mean that organisations can use this as a legal reason to avoid prosecution under vicarious liability laws (Scotland) thereby ensuring all survivors of childhood sexual abuse are viewed with the same rights under the law.

rejection.details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/
